title: DSC extension manifest
description: Defines the information DSC requires to process and surface a DSC extension.

$schema.title: Manifest Schema
$schema.description: This property must be the canonical URL of the Command-based DSC resource Manifest schema that the manifest is implemented for.

version.title: Extension Semantic Version
version.description: The semantic version (semver) of the DSC extension.

description.title: Extension description
description.description: A short synopsis of the DSC extension's purpose.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Defines a list of searchable terms for the extension.

discover.description: Details how to call the Discover method of the extension.

exitCodes.title: Exit codes
exitCodes.description: This property defines a map of valid exit codes for the DSC extension. DSC always interprets exit code `0` as a successful operation and any other exit code as an error. Use this property to indicate human-readable semantic meanings for the DSC extension's exit codes.

secret.description: Details how to call the Secret method of the extension.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.title: DSC extension fully qualified type name
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.description:
The namespaced name of the DSC extension, using the syntax:

<owner>[.<group>][.<area>][.<subarea>]/<name>

For example:

  - Microsoft/Example
  - Microsoft.DSC/Docs
  - Microsoft.Windows.Appx/Discover

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.title: Semantic Version
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.description:
A valid semantic version (semver) string.

For reference, see https://semver.org/
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.$comment:
A valid semantic version ([semver][01]) string.

This value uses the [suggested regular expression][02] to validate whether the string is valid
semver. This is the same pattern, made multi-line for easier readability:

```regex
^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)
(?:-(
  (?:0|[1-9]\d*|\d*[a-zA-Z-][0-9a-zA-Z-]*)
  (?:\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*|\d*[a-zA-Z-][0-9a-zA-Z-]*))
*))?
(?:\+([0-9a-zA-Z-]+(?:\.[0-9a-zA-Z-]+)*))?$
```

The first line matches the `major.minor.patch` components of the version. The middle lines match
the pre-release components. The last line matches the build metadata component.

[01]: https://semver.org/
[02]: https://semver.org/#is-there-a-suggested-regular-expression-regex-to-check-a-semver-string

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.title: Executable Command Name
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.description: The name of the command to run.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.title: Executable Command Arguments
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.description: The list of arguments to pass to the command. The arguments can be any number of strings. If you want to pass the JSON object representing the property bag for the resource to an argument, you can define a single item in the array as a JSON object, indicating the name of the argument with the `jsonInputArg` string property and whether the argument is mandatory for the command with the `mandatory` boolean property.

oneOf.title: String argument
oneOf.description: Any item in the argument array can be a string representing a static argument to pass to the command.

oneOf.title: JSON input argument
oneOf.description: Defines an argument for the command that accepts the JSON input object as a string. DSC passes the JSON input to the named argument when available. You can define the `mandatory` property to indicate whether DSC should always pass the argument to the command, even when there's no JSON input for the command. In that case, DSC passes an empty string to the JSON input argument. You can only define one JSON input argument per arguments array.

jsonInputArg.title: JSON input argument name
jsonInputArg.description: Defines the argument that accepts the JSON property bag for the resource as input.

mandatory.title: Mandatory argument
mandatory.description: Defines whether the argument is mandatory. If this property is set to `true`, DSC passes an empty string when no JSON input is provided. The default value is `false`.

extensionsArg.description: The argument that accepts the extensions list as a comma-separated string.

includeQuotes.description: Whether DSC surrounds the extensions list with quotes.

executable.description: The command to run to get the state of the resource.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PowerS.description: Defines how to call the extension to retrieve a secret from a vault.

allOf.description: The arguments must define exactly one object with the `nameArg` property.
allOf.title: Secret name input argument

allOf.description: The arguments may define at most one object with the `vaultArg` property.
allOf.title: Vault input argument

args.description: The arguments to pass to the command to retrieve a secret. The arguments must define the secret name input argument exactly once and may define the vault input argument at most once.

anyOf.description: A static string argument to pass to the command, like `get` or `--quiet`.

The argument that accepts the secret name. DSC passes the name of the secret to retrieve
after this argument. The arguments must define this argument exactly once.

nameArg.description: The argument that accepts the secret name, like `--name` or `--secret-name`.

anyOf.description:
The argument that accepts the vault name. DSC passes the name of the vault after this
argument when the `secret()` function specifies a vault. The arguments may define this
argument at most once.

vaultArg.description: The argument that accepts the vault name, like `--vault` or `--vault-name`.
